name: Legal
summary: Wills, powers of attorney, health-care directives, guardians for children, titles, and where the papers are kept.
disclaimer: This is a checklist, not legal advice.
intro: What a household needs in place so that someone can act for you, care for your children and find your papers if you cannot. Each line says what "done" means. Where your state publishes its own form, the line links to that state’s page.
groups: If you cannot decide for yourself
Papers and where they are kept

items.title: Make a will that meets your state's signing and witness rules
items.done: Done when each adult's will is signed and witnessed as your state requires and the person it names to settle the estate has agreed to do it.

items.title: In Michigan, make your will with a lawyer or on the Michigan statutory will form
items.done: Done when the will is signed before at least two adult witnesses who also sign, and the personal representative it names has agreed to serve.

form.label: Michigan statutory will (MCL 700.2519, form in statute)

items.title: Sign your will the Illinois way
items.done: Done when the will is in writing, signed by you and attested in your presence by two credible witnesses who are left nothing in it, and the person it names to settle the estate has agreed to do it.

form.label: Illinois State Bar Association: Your Guide to Estate Planning (wills)

items.title: Name a guardian, and a backup, for your children in your will
items.done: Done when each parent's will names a guardian and a backup for the children and both people have said yes.

items.title: Give a trusted adult written authority to care for your children short term
items.done: Done when a signed and dated paper lets a named adult care for and get treatment for your children if you are away, in the hospital or detained, that adult is on every school and childcare pick-up list and holds a copy with the insurance details and the pediatrician's number, and the date the paper runs out is in your calendar.

items.title: In Illinois, appoint a short-term guardian for your children on the statutory form
items.done: Done when the appointment is dated, signed by you before two credible witnesses aged 18 or over, neither of them the guardian you name, signed by that guardian and, where the form calls for it, by the other parent, set to run no longer than 365 days with a calendar reminder to sign a new one, and copied to the guardian and the school or childcare.

form.label: Illinois short-term guardian appointment (755 ILCS 5/11-5.4, form in statute)

items.title: In Michigan, delegate parental powers to a trusted adult by power of attorney
items.done: Done when a signed power of attorney, for no more than 180 days (longer only for a parent deployed abroad with the armed forces), lets a named adult care for your children, that adult is on every school and childcare pick-up list and has a copy, and the date it runs out is in your calendar with a reminder to sign a new one.

items.group: If you cannot decide for yourself
items.title: Sign a durable power of attorney for money and property
items.done: Done when each adult has a signed durable power of attorney naming an agent and a backup, signed in the way your state requires, and the agent has a copy.

items.group: If you cannot decide for yourself
items.title: In Illinois, sign the statutory short form power of attorney for property
items.done: Done when the agent has a copy and the form is signed before one witness and a notary who is a different person, neither of them an agent, your doctor or mental-health provider, or a parent, sibling or descendant of you or your agent, and every witness meets the limits printed on the form itself.

form.label: Illinois Statutory Short Form Power of Attorney for Property (Illinois Department on Aging)

items.group: If you cannot decide for yourself
items.title: In Michigan, sign a durable power of attorney under the Uniform Power of Attorney Act
items.done: Done when the agent has a copy and the power of attorney, signed by you in person, is acknowledged before a notary or signed before two witnesses who also sign and are not agents named in it (a power that someone else signs at your direction always needs the two witnesses).

form.label: Michigan statutory form power of attorney (MCL 556.401, form in statute)

items.group: If you cannot decide for yourself
items.title: Name a health-care agent who can decide for you if you cannot
items.done: Done when each adult has a signed health-care power of attorney or proxy naming an agent and a backup, and the agent and your doctor each have a copy.

items.group: If you cannot decide for yourself
items.title: In Illinois, sign the statutory short form power of attorney for health care
items.done: Done when the agent you name is not your own health-care provider, your agent and doctor have copies, and the form is signed before a witness aged 18 or over who is not an agent, a relative of you or your agent, or your doctor or another health professional named on the form, and every witness meets the limits printed on the form itself.

form.label: Illinois Statutory Short Form Power of Attorney for Health Care (IDPH)

items.group: If you cannot decide for yourself
items.title: In Michigan, sign a patient advocate designation
items.done: Done when the designation is signed before two qualifying witnesses, your patient advocate has signed the acceptance, and a copy is in your medical record.

items.group: If you cannot decide for yourself
items.title: Write down the treatment you would or would not want at the end of life
items.done: Done when each adult who wants one has a signed living will or treatment-wishes statement that agrees with what their health-care agent has been told.

items.group: If you cannot decide for yourself
items.title: In Illinois, sign a living will declaration if you want one
items.done: Done when your doctor has been told and given a copy, and the declaration is signed before two witnesses aged 18 or over who did not sign for you, would inherit nothing from you and are not paying for your medical care, neither of them your health-care professional, and every witness meets the limits printed on the form itself.

items.group: If you cannot decide for yourself
items.title: Record your wishes for mental-health treatment, if your state allows it
items.done: Done when anyone who wants one has a signed mental-health treatment declaration or directive and the person it names has accepted in writing.

items.group: If you cannot decide for yourself
items.title: In Illinois, sign a declaration for mental health treatment if you want one
items.done: Done when the declaration is signed before two qualifying witnesses, any attorney-in-fact has accepted in writing, and a renewal date three years on is in your calendar.

form.label: Illinois Declaration for Mental Health Treatment (IDPH)

items.group: If you cannot decide for yourself
items.title: In Michigan, give your patient advocate authority over mental-health treatment
items.done: Done when your patient advocate designation says in writing whether your advocate may make mental-health treatment decisions, and what you want.

form.label: Michigan designation of patient advocate, medical or mental health treatment (MCL 700.5506)

items.done: Done when copies of the deed or lease for your home and the title and registration for each vehicle are with your documents.

items.title: Find out how the deed to your home is titled and who it passes to
items.done: Done when you have read the deed, know whose names are on it and in what form of ownership, and have written that on the legal papers list.

items.title: Find out whether your state lets your home pass by a transfer-on-death deed
items.done: Done when the legal papers list shows, for your home, either the date the deed was recorded or the words “not using one” and your reason.

items.title: In Illinois, decide whether to record a transfer on death instrument for your home
items.done: Done when the legal papers list shows your choice and, if you use one, it is signed by you before two credible witnesses, neither of them a beneficiary or a beneficiary's spouse, your signature and theirs are acknowledged before a notary, and it is recorded with the county recorder before your death.

form.label: Illinois Real Property Transfer on Death Instrument Act, requirements (755 ILCS 27/40)

items.title: If you own your home in Michigan, ask a lawyer whether an enhanced life estate (“Lady Bird”) deed fits it
items.done: Done when a Michigan lawyer has answered that question and the legal papers list shows, for your home, either the date the deed was recorded or the words “not using one” and your reason.

form.label: State Bar of Michigan, Michigan Bar Journal: Ladybird deeds, key features and uses

items.title: If you own a vehicle, check how it is titled and how it would pass if you died
items.done: Done when the legal papers list shows, for each vehicle, the names on the paper title and the form your state's motor-vehicle agency needs after a death.

items.title: In Illinois, decide whether to name a beneficiary on each vehicle title
items.done: Done when the legal papers list says, for each vehicle, either the date a Beneficiary Affidavit was filed with the Secretary of State or “none, on purpose”.

form.label: Illinois Secretary of State: Beneficiary Affidavit (VSD 773)

items.title: In Michigan, check whether each vehicle title carries “Full Rights to Survivor”
items.done: Done when you have looked at each paper title and written on the legal papers list whose names are on it and whether it carries the words “Full Rights to Survivor”.

form.label: Michigan Secretary of State: Titles (see “Deceased owner”)

items.group: Papers and where they are kept
items.done: Done when a copy of each will, power of attorney and directive is with your documents and your executor knows where the signed originals are.

items.group: Papers and where they are kept
items.done: Done when copies of marriage, divorce and custody papers are with your documents, and the legal papers list says where each original is kept.

items.group: Papers and where they are kept
items.done: Done when copies of adoption, citizenship and immigration papers are with your documents and the originals are in a fire- and water-resistant place.

items.group: Papers and where they are kept
items.title: Decide who besides you can open your safe-deposit box
items.done: Done when you have checked your rental agreement, added a joint renter if you want one, and told your executor where the box and its key are.

items.group: Papers and where they are kept
items.title: Keep each signed original where your agents can reach it when it is needed
items.done: Done when every original is in a place your agents and executor can get to quickly, with powers of attorney and health directives kept out of a bank box.

items.group: Papers and where they are kept
items.title: In Michigan, consider depositing your will with your county probate court
items.done: Done when you have decided where the original will is kept and, if you deposit it with the probate court, the certificate of deposit is with your documents.

form.label: Michigan deposit of will for safekeeping (MCL 700.2515)

items.group: Papers and where they are kept
items.title: Fill in the legal papers list and tell your agents where it is
items.done: Done when the legal papers list shows each document, who it names, the date signed and where the original is, and your agents know where the list is kept.

Done when three separate things are in place: a power of attorney or the bank's own authority form so that someone can act if you cannot, a trusted contact on each account that offers one for fraud concerns only (a trusted contact cannot move money or act for you), and each main account's legacy or inactive-account setting for after a death.
Done when current recovery codes for your email, cloud storage, password manager and bank are printed and kept in your fire chest at home, never in the document pouch.

items.title: Say in your will or power of attorney who may handle your digital accounts
items.done: Done when your will or power of attorney says whether your agent or executor may access your online accounts, and any account settings you use agree with it.

items.title: Put in writing who will decide on your burial or cremation
items.done: Done when you have signed your state's form naming a person, and a backup, to make funeral and burial or cremation decisions, and they have a copy.

items.title: In Illinois, appoint an agent to control disposition of your remains
items.done: Done when an appointment in the statutory form is signed and notarized, your agent has signed to accept, and your agent has a copy.

form.label: Illinois Appointment of Agent to Control Disposition of Remains (755 ILCS 65/10, form in statute)

items.title: In Michigan, designate a funeral representative
items.done: Done when a dated, signed designation naming your funeral representative is witnessed by two qualifying adults or notarized, and the representative has a copy.

items.title: Review every legal paper after a move, marriage, divorce, birth or death
items.done: Done when after each move, marriage, divorce, birth or death, every affected will, power of attorney, directive, title and deed has been reviewed and updated or re-signed where necessary.

items.title: If a power of attorney or health directive you hold was signed under another state's law, ask whether it works where you live, bank and get care
items.done: Done when, for each such paper, a lawyer or legal aid office has told you whether it is honored in each state where you live, bank and get care, and the answer is on the legal papers list.

items.title: Find a lawyer or free legal aid service you could call
items.done: Done when the phone number of a lawyer, lawyer-referral service or legal aid office is on your legal papers list.
